title: Cleaning versus disinfection
moduleTitle: Shared: Job management and service delivery
audience: Trainee or new worker on the window cleaning (all heights) track, working under supervision.
learningOutcomes: Explain and demonstrate cleaning versus disinfection

instruction.heading: Exterior, height and access context
instruction.body: This lesson is part of the window cleaning (all heights) track. The track covers ground-level, water-fed pole and elevated access work on glazing and frames. Any work above ground level, or from a ladder, scaffold or elevating work platform, is restricted: it needs employer authorisation under a site-specific risk assessment, and the worker must hold any licence the relevant state or territory requires for the equipment used. This lesson does not grant the right to work at height or on solar systems.

instruction.heading: Instruction
instruction.body: Cleaning physically removes soil and reduces contamination; disinfection uses an approved product or process to inactivate targeted microorganisms on suitable surfaces. Determine whether disinfection is required from the work scope, risk assessment and site protocol. When required, remove visible soil first unless the product specifically supports a validated one-step method. Read the label for approved surfaces, dilution, application method, wet contact time and rinsing requirements, especially on food-contact surfaces. Do not substitute a household product for a healthcare-grade requirement. Never promise that a surface is sterile after routine cleaning.

instruction.heading: Learning focus
instruction.body: Choose cleaning and disinfection appropriately. Cleaning physically removes soil and reduces contamination; disinfection uses an approved product or process to inactivate targeted microorganisms on suitable surfaces. Determine whether disinfection is required from the work scope, risk assessment and site protocol. When required, remove visible soil first unless the product specifically supports a validated one-step method. Read the label for approved surfaces, dilution, application method, wet contact time and rinsing requirements, especially on food-contact surfaces. Do not substitute a household product for a healthcare-grade requirement. Never promise that a surface is sterile after routine cleaning.

instruction.heading: Worked workplace scenario
instruction.body: A team wipes a high-touch surface with disinfectant and dries it immediately. The assessor asks them to check the actual label contact time and repeat the approved process if necessary.

instruction.heading: Guided practice
instruction.body: Given three scenarios, justify cleaning alone or cleaning plus disinfection, and demonstrate label-based preparation and contact-time compliance.

instruction.heading: Quality and safety checks
instruction.body: Before signing off, confirm that the method matches the authorised site scope and current product labels, that no uncontrolled hazard remains, and that evidence is factual and privacy-safe.

instruction.heading: Stop-work rule
instruction.body: Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

procedure: Decide from the work scope, risk assessment and site protocol whether disinfection is required, or whether cleaning alone is enough.
Read the product label for approved surfaces, dilution, application method, wet contact time and rinsing requirements.
Remove visible soil first, unless the label supports a validated one-step method.
Apply the product using the label's approved dilution and application method.
Keep the surface wet for the label's wet contact time before wiping or drying it.
Rinse where the label requires it, especially on food-contact surfaces.
Use a healthcare-grade product where the requirement calls for one, and do not substitute a household product.
Confirm the method matches the authorised scope before sign-off, and do not describe the surface as sterile after routine cleaning.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Licence and height notice: This lesson does not grant the right to work at height, on roofs, from elevated work platforms, or on solar systems. Completing it is not a licence, certificate or authority for regulated work. Boom-type elevating work platforms need a high risk work licence in Victoria at any boom length, and in New South Wales, Queensland, Tasmania, the Northern Territory and Western Australia where the boom is 11 metres or more. The WorkSafe WA page (last updated 13 August 2026) and the NT WorkSafe bulletin (no date shown) both state the 11-metre threshold. Check whether this work needs a high-risk work licence with the state regulator before you start. Queensland's definition does not cover platforms under 11 metres (WorkSafe Queensland page, no date shown). Tasmania's WP licence applies where the boom length is 11 metres or more, and no licence is needed for a boom under 11 metres (WorkSafe Tasmania page, last updated 1 December 2023). In New South Wales and Queensland the boom length is 11 metres: a boom-type platform of 11 metres or more needs the licence, and a shorter boom may not need it in those states. Victoria's WP class has no boom-length threshold, so the licence is not limited by length there. This lesson does not grant a licence. Scissor lifts need no high risk work licence in Victoria or the Northern Territory. Check the licence rules for your state or territory and obtain your employer's written authorisation before any work above ground level.

Stop-work rule: stop immediately, make the area safe, and tell your supervisor before resuming if the surface, anchor, ladder, platform or roof is unstable or uncertain; wind, rain, ice or fading light changes conditions; you see or suspect exposed wiring, damaged cable, water near electrical equipment or live parts; a person or animal enters the exclusion zone; the task falls outside your training, authorisation or the work order; or you are asked to work above ground level without the licence or authorisation required.

qualityStandard: Disinfection is used only where the work scope, risk assessment or site protocol requires it.
Visible soil is removed before disinfection, unless the label supports a validated one-step method.
The label's approved surfaces, dilution, application, wet contact time and rinsing requirements are followed, especially on food-contact surfaces.
A household product is never substituted for a healthcare-grade requirement.
summary: Cleaning physically removes soil, while disinfection uses an approved product or process to inactivate targeted microorganisms on suitable surfaces.
The work scope, risk assessment and site protocol decide whether disinfection is needed, and visible soil is removed first unless the product supports a validated one-step method.
The label sets the approved surfaces, dilution, application method, wet contact time and rinsing, and a household product is not used in place of a healthcare-grade requirement.

knowledgeChecks.question: What must be checked before deciding whether a surface needs disinfection?
options: Whether a household product can be substituted for a healthcare-grade need in the ward and the room today
Whether the scope, risk assessment and site protocol require disinfection, and the label's surfaces, dilution and contact time
Whether the client expects the surface to be sterile afterwards after the job, the clean and the wipe
Whether the surface can be dried immediately after wiping it down with the cloth, the spray and the rag

knowledgeChecks.question: What should you do when a surface needs disinfecting but the product is not approved?
options: Keep working and note it on the next label for the product used on the job
Repeat the disinfection with a stronger product on the same surface
Stop, and escalate the uncontrolled hazard or unauthorised task to the supervisor
Proceed, since the client has approved the task verbally on the day

knowledgeChecks.question: When must visible soil be removed first before disinfecting?
options: Always, unless the product specifically supports a validated one-step method
